office_does: The County Assessor sets the taxable value of property in Clark County and runs the property-tax exemption programs; levy amounts are set by taxing districts and voters.
race_blurb: Four-term Assessor Peter Van Nortwick, who points to his work expanding the senior property-tax exemption, faces real estate investor Tyler Thoune, who argues the office under-assesses expensive homes and loses too many appeals. Neither campaign has raised much money and no news coverage of the race was found.

candidates.summary: Clark County Assessor since 2011 and a certified general appraiser, running on his exemption advocacy and a leaner office.
highlights: Says he fought in Olympia to expand the senior exemption, whose income threshold rises to $85,000 [S1]
Supports a state homestead exemption for property-tax relief [S1]
Says the office now runs with fewer full-time employees than when he was first elected [S1]

experience.basis: Four-term incumbent running on his credentials and record in the office.

taxes.basis: Advocates property-tax relief through expanded senior and new homestead exemptions.

spending.basis: Emphasizes fewer staff and low costs; in 2019 he did seek temporary staff for exemption workload.

candidates.summary: Real estate investor and remodeler with more than 20 years in the Clark County market, running on assessment accuracy and fairness between property owners.
highlights: Says a $13.5 million home sold days before the valuation date was assessed at about 44% of its price [S1]
Says 56% of 2024 valuation appeals reaching the Board of Equalization were reduced or overturned [S1]
Promises fair valuations, transparency and accountability for mistakes [S1]

experience.basis: No elected or government experience; runs on outside market experience against a four-term incumbent.
